hypothesis: Does tonight's champion recipe (PGO + THP) transfer off Graviton5? Same build on i8g (Graviton4, Neoverse V2), measured against its own same-boot control. On m9g the pair is worth -8.7%; a similar figure here makes it a property of the workload and the ARM core family rather than of one chip.
llm_commentary: The champion recipe transfers off Graviton5 and pays more on Graviton4: i8g 6.61s [6.59/6.68/6.57] → 5.80s [5.77/5.93/5.69], -12.3% with disjoint ranges, against m9g's -8.7% for the same PGO+THP pair. So the win is a property of the workload and the ARM core family, not of one chip, and the older/slower core benefits most — consistent with the rest of this project's pattern, where every lever that removes per-operation overhead or improves locality has paid more on Neoverse V2 than on V3 or Zen 5. The same build also needed the same two aarch64 PGO fixes (explicit --target, lld for the instrumented link), so the recipe in knowledge/workload/reth/pgo-on-reth.md is portable as written. A closing control is in flight to bracket this delta.
